question: Do Kodak's first-party TRI-X 400 contrast-index curves contain developer-specific process shape that cannot be reduced to one common contrast response plus a scalar development-time shift?

source.title: KODAK PROFESSIONAL TRI-X 320 and 400 Films
source.film: KODAK PROFESSIONAL TRI-X 400 Film / 400TX, 35 mm and 120-size

analysis.common_time_shift_control: subtract each developer's mean log development time over the four shared contrast indices
analysis.uncertainty: recompute every signature under all coherent axis-aligned plus/minus maximum-source-pixel-error translations of each complete vector path; compare observed separation to the resulting worst-case coordinate-registration envelope; this does not bound manufacturer measurement error

forbidden: treat development time recommendations as calibrated photographic appearance
infer HP5 Plus versus TRI-X stock differences from asymmetric source curves
fit a photographic renderer, grain, MTF, scanner or print profile
change AO6 or any product default
move trace points, change shared contrast indices or relax gates after scoring

branch_rule.pass: retain developer identity as an explicit required B&W FilmProfileBundle dimension and next test only a typed monotone process-response representation
branch_rule.fail: retain developer/process as unknown metadata but do not compile distinct response profiles from this source

claim_ceiling: First-party TRI-X 400 diffuse-visual contrast-index source evidence about developer/process separability; not a scanned-image look, stock comparison, roll calibration, grain/MTF/scanner evidence or product profile.
